problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 8 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(11{v}_{1}+6{v}_{2}).$
worked_solution:
First, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}11{v}_{1}+6{v}_{2} & =11{v}_{1}+11{v}_{2}-5{v}_{2} \\  & =11({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})-5{v}_{2} \\  & =11(0)-5{v}_{2} \\  & =-5{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(11{v}_{1}+6{v}_{2})=T(-5{v}_{2}).
$$

 

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-5{v}_{2}) & =-5T({v}_{2}) \\  & =-5[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 8 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-35 \\ -40 \\ -45\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(11{v}_{1}+6{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-35 \\ -40 \\ -45\end{aligned}].$
